tier_reason: Stays A (public harness, flags and CPU in the repo's benchmark docs). Enricher caveat correction: the libevent 4096-byte read limit is still the default in 2.1.12-stable, and the charted client run is ambiguous.

corrections.caveats: Numbers read from chart PNGs; the big-message win comes from libevent's hard-coded 4096-byte read limit (EVBUFFER_MAX_READ), still the default in 2.1.12-stable (master adds evbuffer_set_max_read()), so the gap is a libevent default rather than a faster core; evpp is 3% slower at 1 connection with 16 KiB messages and the 8192-byte gain is 22-42%, below the claimed 40-130%. single_thread.sh runs client.cc and then client_fixed_size.cc against one server per cell and the doc never says which run was charted, while the libevent script runs only the streaming client; the baseline is libevent's bufferevent sample and raw libevent is about 2% faster than evpp. Abandoned: last release v0.7.0 2017-07-13, last commit 2022-11-06, #303 heap-use-after-free open.

tier_reason: Stays C (vendor snippets only). Enricher caveat correction: the compared built-in stack lacked a TCP retransmission queue, congestion control and out-of-order handling, so it is not like-for-like with lwIP.

corrections.caveats: Vendor first-party claim seen only as search snippets (mongoose.ws and the EEVblog post blocked): 1080 req/s Mongoose vs 286 lwIP raw vs 16 lwIP sockets on a Nucleo-F746ZG, with no public bench code, compiler, flags or lwIP tuning; snippets disagree on the lwIP figures (286 vs 16 req/s, Zephyr sockets 3 req/s). The built-in Mongoose TCP/IP stack measured there kept no TCP retransmission queue (MG_ENABLE_TCPIP_TCPRTX 0, sent bytes deleted on send; the optional queue arrived with PR #3682 on 2026-09-08), has no congestion control, drops out-of-order segments and uses a fixed 6000-byte window, so it did less work than lwIP raw. The linked page carries footprint only (flash 50,140 vs 67,020 B, RAM 22,524 vs 31,504 B). Issue #3507 (silent WebSocket data loss over GSM/LTE on 7.21); 10 GitHub advisories including 2 critical request-smuggling ones. GPL-2.0 or commercial.
